body:
“The HipHop Declaration of Peace,” ⓐpresenting to
the UN on May 16th, 2001, officially recognized
hip-hop as a (A)[domestic / worldwide] culture of
peace. This document reminds us ⓑthat hip-hop’s
original mission to bring peace to the Bronx,
implying global respect for hip-hop history. When
hip-hop artist Kendrick Lamar ⓒwas awarded a
Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2018, it was another
important event. It meant that hip-hop, ⓓwhich
started as (B)[mainstream / underground] music, had
become a major art form like classical music.
If hip-hop music was born as part of a cultural
movement for peace in the 1970s, today more and
more people regard it as a powerful means to
express oneself, fight against injustice, bring about
change through social messages, and still be
engaged with music and ⓔconnected to others.
With its unique and (C)[diminishing / expanding]
appeal, hip-hop continues to be a global phenomenon.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: worldwide underground  expanding
worldwide mainstream  expanding
domestic mainstream  expanding
worldwide underground  diminishing
domestic mainstream  diminishing
solution: (A) ‘힙합 평화 선언문’이 2001년 5월 16일에 유엔에 제출되었 다고 했으므로, 힙합을 국제적인 평화 문화로 공식 인정했다는 흐름이 되는 worldwide(전 세계적인)가 알맞다. (B) 앞서 힙합 아티스트 Kendrick Lamar가 2018년 퓰리처 음악 상을 수상한 것이 또 하나의 중요한 사건이었다고 했으며, 뒤에 는 힙합이 클래식 음악 같은 주요 예술 형식으로 자리 잡았다 는 내용이 이어지므로, 힙합이 원래는 비주류의 음악으로 시작 되었다는 흐름이 되는 underground(언더그라운드의)가 알맞다. (C) 오늘날 점점 더 많은 사람들이 힙합을 자신을 표현하고 불 의에 맞서 싸우고 사회적 메시지를 통해 변화를 가져오는 것 등을 위한 강력한 수단으로 여기고 있으며, 힙합은 계속해서 세계적인 현상이 되고 있다는 내용이 이어지므로, 힙합의 독특 함과 더욱 커지는 매력을 언급하는 흐름으로 expanding(확대 되는)이 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

body:
Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of
early hip-hop, typically ⓐfocusing on having a good
time together and boasting about the ability of the
DJ or the rapper. However, a significant shift
occurred during the (A)[rise / decline] of hip-hop
music in the 1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The Message by the group
Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five in 1982 ⓑwas
groundbreaking. This song’s powerful lyrics detailed
the harsh realities of life in the ghetto, including
the sad story of a boy who was born there and
had to live and die as a second-class citizen. With
this song, hip-hop, whose original aim was
ⓒcreating peace through partying, started a new
tradition of social criticism against injustice. The
Message became one of the most influential rap
singles of all time, and was followed by many
hip-hop songs that (B)[supported / confronted]
racial discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the
same time, their music with its rhythmic beat and
rapping made people ⓓto move or dance. People
heard the social message while moving to the beat.
Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop
lyrics, which can be summarized as “respect.”
Hip-hop music began to be a way to express
respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop
pioneers. For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who
overcame hardship and injustice and went on to
create new music and culture. Therefore, many
hip-hoppers agree ⓔthat they cannot have too
much respect for these heroes. The phrase
“something from nothing,” often used to summarize
the genre’s history, is also an expression of
(C)[admiration / hatred] for early hip-hoppers, who
developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very
limited resources. Rappers also proudly expressed
their feeling that they, too, and perhaps the
audience, ⓕhad suffered and survived in a similar
way to the pioneers. This is why (D)__________________
_______________________________________________________.
The importance of the idea of respect in hip-hop
cannot ⓖemphasize strongly enough.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: risesupportedhatred
riseconfrontedadmiration
declinesupportedhatred
riseconfrontedhatred
declineconfrontedadmiration
solution: (A) 노래 <The message(메시지)>의 등장을 계기로 이후 1980 년대와 1990년대에 사회 비판의 메시지를 담은 많은 힙합 노 래가 뒤를 이었다는 내용이 글에 언급되므로, 1980년대 힙합의 부상 시기에 중요한 변화가 일어났다는 흐름이 되는 rise(대두, 부상)가 알맞다. (B) 노래 <The message(메시지)>를 통해 불의에 저항하는 새 로운 사회 비판의 전통을 시작했다는 내용에 이어지므로, 이후 인종 차별에 맞서는 힙합 노래들이 뒤를 이었다는 흐름이 되 는 confronted(~에 맞섰다)가 알맞다. (C) 많은 힙합인들이 고난과 불의를 딛고 나아가 새로운 음악 과 문화를 창조해 낸 힙합 선구자들에게 아무리 큰 존경심을 가져도 지나치지 않다는 데 동의한다고 했으므로, ‘무에서 유 를’이라는 어구가 제한된 자원에도 불구하고 새로운 문화를 일 구어 낸 초기 힙합인들에 대한 존경의 표현이라는 흐름이 되 는 admiration(존경)이 알맞다.

body:
A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final
sound of a word. Most often, it is (A)[consciously /
unintentionally] used for a musical effect in the final
position of lines within poems or songs. Let’s look
at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.
First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this
is called an end rhyme, which is the most
representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the
following example aloud.
My house is so big you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an
ending sound “op.”
Second, words can rhyme within the same line.
This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a
word in the middle of a line and another word in
the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn
Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For
example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not
exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of
(B)[similar / dissimilar] sounds /s/ and /t/. In most
imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while
the vowel sounds are different, or ⓐthe other way
round.
When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken
aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This
helps the song keep a steady beat, (C)[offends /
pleases] the ear, and evokes emotions. So, if you
create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your
voice stronger and reach your listeners.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: consciously      dissimilar    pleases
unintentionally      similar    pleases
consciously      similar    offends
unintentionally      dissimilar    offends
consciously      similar    pleases
solution: (A) 라임은 시나 노래에서 음악적 효과를 주기 위해 사용된다 는 내용이 이어지므로, 라임이 의도적으로 사용된다는 흐름이 되는 consciously(의식적으로)가 알맞다. (B) ‘start’, ‘sport’, ‘straight’는 비슷한 /s/ 소리 및 /t/ 소리의 패턴을 만드는 단어들의 예시이므로, 이 세 단어들이 정확히 라임을 이루진 않지만 유사한 /s/ 소리 및 /t/ 소리의 패턴을 만든다는 흐름이 되는 similar(유사한)가 알맞다. (C) 라임을 이루는 일련의 단어들을 큰 소리로 말하면 리듬감 있는 패턴 또는 ‘흐름’이 만들어지며, 이는 노래가 안정된 박자를 유지하도록 돕는다는 내용에 이어지므로, 듣는 이의 귀를 즐겁 게 한다는 흐름이 되는 pleases(~을 기쁘게 하다)가 알맞다.

body:
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. Abandoned
buildings and parking lots ⓐ[used / were used] for
events called block parties. What eventually
emerged from these parties? A vibrant youth
movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing,
breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang
violence with music, dance, art, and style.
The most popular block parties were those hosted
by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding
father of hip-hop. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday
in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of
hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At
this party, using two turntables at the same time,
Herc played two copies of the same record and
then switched between them to extend the drum
section known as the break. No longer ⓑ[people
had / did people have] to stop dancing at the end
of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.
Kool Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential
in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and ⓒ[use / using] the break to show off their
individual dancing skills. Kool Herc named the
people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls,
short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people
began to dance in groups in the streets and build
a street dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the
crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the beat”
and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning of
rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both DJing
and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked
a friend to take the role of addressing the audience,
that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their
parties. This separate role became MCing.

After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. Abandoned
buildings and parking lots ⓐ[used / were used] for
events called block parties. What eventually
emerged from these parties? A vibrant youth
movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing,
breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang
violence with music, dance, art, and style.
The most popular block parties were those hosted
by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding
father of hip-hop. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday
in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of
hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At
this party, using two turntables at the same time,
Herc played two copies of the same record and
then switched between them to extend the drum
section known as the break. No longer ⓑ[people
had / did people have] to stop dancing at the end
of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.
Kool Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential
in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and ⓒ[use / using] the break to show off their
individual dancing skills. Kool Herc named the
people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls,
short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people
began to dance in groups in the streets and build
a street dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the
crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the beat”
and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning of
rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both DJing
and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked
a friend to take the role of addressing the audience,
that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their
parties. This separate role became MCing.

Imagine an urban area ⓐthat is fast becoming a
slum after an economic recession. Businesses close
their doors and building owners have left. The area
is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating
even in winter. Only those who can’t afford to move
out remain. Unemployment is high, many gangs
emerge, and gang violence between young people
ⓑbecome an everyday thing. Despair is on every
street corner. One day, however, a gang called the
Ghetto Brothers, which is respected because of its
free meal and medical care programs, decides to
stop fighting and instead persuade young people
ⓒto unite and create a better community. They
suggest a peace treaty. “This is for peace, men. The
violence took away our brothers. We’re not gangsters
anymore. We’ve got to make this town a better
place to live.” Thanks to these new voices, gang
leaders from all over the area sign the treaty. Never
again will they use violence to solve their disputes.
This is the Bronx in the New York of the early
1970s, ⓓwhich hip-hop music was born as a major
part of a new culture of peace created by African
Americans and immigrants. The story of hip-hop,
now one of the world’s most dominant music
genres, is a ⓔfascinating one. Let’s explore it.

Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of
early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good
time together and boasting about the ability of the
DJ or the rapper. ⓐ______________, a significant shift
occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the
1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The
Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and
Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This
song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of
life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy
who was born there and had to live and die as a
second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose
original aim was creating peace through partying,
started a new tradition of social criticism against
injustice. The Message became one of the most
influential rap singles of all time, and was followed
by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial
discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same
time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping
made people move or dance. People heard the
social message while moving to the beat.
Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop
lyrics, which can be summarized as “respect.”
Hip-hop music began to be a way to express
respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop
pioneers. For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who
overcame hardship and injustice and went on to
create new music and culture. ⓑ_____________, many
hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much
respect for these heroes. The phrase “something
from nothing,” often used to summarize the genre’s
history, is also an expression of admiration for early
hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the
ghetto despite very limited resources. Rappers also
proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and
perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in
a similar way to the pioneers. This is why the
message of respect is about both self-worth and
respect for others. ⓒ힙합에서 존경이라는 개념의 중
요성은 아무리 강하게 강조해도 지나치지 않다.

body:
A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final sound of a word. Most often, it is consciously used for a musical effect in the final position of lines within poems or songs. Let’s look at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.

First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this is called an end rhyme, which is the most representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the following example aloud.
My house is so big that you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an ending sound “op.”

Second, words can rhyme within the same line. This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a word in the middle of a line and another word in the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn

Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are different, or the other way round.

When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear, and evokes emotions. So, if you create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger and reach your listeners.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Why Rhyming Matters in Rap Lyrics
Perfect Rhymes: The Key to Successful Rap
How Rappers Come Up with Great Rhymes
The Types and Effects of Rhymes in Rap Lyrics
The Emotional Power of Rhyming in Rap Lyrics

2. 마지막 문단에서 라임이 리듬(flow)을 만들고 귀를 즐겁게 하며 감정을 불러일으키는 효과를 설명한다.
3. 따라서 제목은 ‘랩 가사 속 라임의 종류와 효과’이다. ①·⑤는 효과만, ③은 라임을 만드는 방법, ②는 완전한 라임만 다뤄 글의 일부이거나 글에 없는 내용이다.
4. 따라서 답은 ④이다.

body:
Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a
slum after ⓐan economic recession. Businesses
close their doors and building owners have left. The
area is full of abandoned buildings. There is no
heating even in winter. Only those who can’t afford
to move out remain. Unemployment is high, many
gangs emerge, and gang violence between young
people becomes ⓑa rare occurrence. Despair is on
every street corner. One day, however, a gang
called the Ghetto Brothers, which is respected
because of its free meal and medical care
programs, decides to stop fighting and instead
persuade young people to unite and create a better
community. They suggest ⓒa peace treaty. “This is
for peace, men. The violence took away our
brothers. We’re not gangsters anymore. We’ve got
to make this town ⓓa better place to live.” Thanks
to these new voices, gang leaders from all over the
area sign the treaty. (A)________________________________
__________________________________________ to solve their
disputes.
This is the Bronx in the New York of the early
1970s, where hip-hop music was born as a major
part of a new culture of peace created by African
Americans and immigrants. The story of hip-hop,
now one of the world’s most dominant music
genres, is ⓔan intriguing one. Let’s explore it.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: No longer will they strive to avoid violence
They will refuse to negotiate with rival gangs
Never again will they seek nonviolent solutions
From now on, they will never resort to violence
They will not seek peaceful cooperation amongyoung people
solution: Ghetto Brothers라는 한 갱단이 싸움을 멈추고 더 나은 공동체 를 만들자고 설득하기로 결정하고, 이런 목소리에 힘입어 지역 전역의 갱단 대표들이 협정에 서명한다고 했으므로, 그들은 결 코 다시는 분쟁 해결에 폭력을 사용하지 않을 것이라는 흐름 으로 빈칸에는 ❹ ‘이제부터, 그들은 절대 폭력에 기대지 않을 것이다’가 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

body:
Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of
early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good
time together and boasting about the ability of the
DJ or the rapper. However, a significant shift
occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the
1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The
Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and
Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This
song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of
life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy
who was born there and had to live and die as a
second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose
original aim was _______________________________________,
started a new tradition of social criticism against
injustice. The Message became one of the most
influential rap singles of all time, and was followed
by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial
discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same
time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping
made people move or dance. People heard the
social message while moving to the beat.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: encouraging competition through partying
using music primarily to reveal racial inequality
urging rappers to concentrate on recent politicalissues
bringing about peace through shared music anddancing
resolving conflicts among generations by meansof parties
solution: 초기 힙합의 파티 구호로 출발한 랩 가사는 일반적으로 다 함 께 즐거운 시간을 갖자는 내용과 디제이나 래퍼의 능력을 뽐 내는 내용에 초점을 두었다고 했으므로, 힙합의 본래 목표는 파티에서 음악과 춤을 통해 평화를 창조하는 것이었다는 흐름 으로 빈칸에는 ❹ ‘공유된 음악과 춤을 통해 평화를 가져오는 것’이 알맞다.

Good morning, students! Today, we’re going to
learn about “pop culture.” First, popular culture, also
called mass culture or pop culture, refers to ideas,
practices, and trends that are popular and
widespread in everyday life. Second, it includes
movies, music, fashion, and dance.
(A) Whether it’s driving changes in fashion or starting
a social movement, pop culture, which spreads
through mass media and online platforms, leaves
a lasting impact.
(B) A good example is the “Ice Bucket Challenge,”
which evolved into a global fundraising event. In
short, pop culture isn’t just about what’s “cool.”
It’s a mirror of society, reflecting and shaping
who we are.
(C) Even online contents such as webtoons, streaming
series, and social media challenges have become
popular genres in pop culture. Third, pop culture
significantly influences our society.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

“The HipHop Declaration of Peace,” presented to
the UN on May 16th, 2001, officially recognized
hip-hop as an international culture of peace. This
document reminds us of hip-hop’s original mission
to bring peace to the Bronx, implying global
respect for hip-hop history. When hip-hop artist
Kendrick Lamar was awarded a Pulitzer Prize for
Music in 2018, it was another important event. It
meant that hip-hop, which started as underground
music, __________________________________________________.
If hip-hop music was born as part of a cultural
movement for peace in the 1970s, today more and
more people regard it as a powerful means to
express oneself, fight against injustice, bring about
change through social messages, and still be
engaged with music and connected to others. With
its unique and growing appeal, hip-hop continues
to be a global phenomenon.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: had gradually diminished in artistic quality
had gained recognition as a significant form ofart
had fallen short of the status achieved byclassical music
had preserved its position outside the world ofmainstream art
had become a genre enjoyed by a small groupof devoted fans
solution: 힙합 아티스트 Kendrick Lamar가 2018년 퓰리처 음악상을 수상 한 것은 또 하나의 주요한 사건이었다는 내용 뒤에 이어져 있으 며, 뒤에서는 오늘날 힙합이 자기표현 등을 위한 강력한 수단으 로 여겨지고 있고 그 독특함과 커지는 매력으로 인해 계속해서 세계적인 현상이 되고 있다고 설명하므로, Kendrick Lamar의 수 상은 언더그라운드 음악으로 출발했던 힙합이 이제 주류 예술로 서 자리 잡았다는 것을 의미한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❷ ‘중요한 예술 형식으로 인정을 받았다’가 알맞다.

body:
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. Abandoned
buildings and parking lots were used for events
called block parties. What eventually emerged from
these parties? A ⓐvibrant youth movement called
hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing,
MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with
music, dance, art, and style.
(A)가장 인기 있는 블록 파티들은 디제이 Kool Herc
에 의해 주최된 것들이었고, 그는 힙합의 창시자로 간
주된다. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday in
August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of
hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At
this party, using two turntables at the same time,
Herc played two copies of the same record and
then switched between them to ⓑreduce the drum
section known as the break. No longer did people
have to stop dancing at the end of the record
while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool Herc’s style
of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of
hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and use the break to show off their individual
dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing
to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, ⓒshort for
Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to
dance in groups in the streets and build a street
dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over ⓓinstrumental parts of songs to excite
the crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the
beat” and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning
of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both
DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they
asked a friend to take the role of (B)________________
________________________, that is, of the Master of
Ceremonies or MC, at their parties. This ⓔseparate
role became MCing.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: changing records
teaching how to rap
organizing block parties
addressing the audience
coordinating dancers’ movements
solution: Kool Herc와 같은 디제이들이 관중의 흥을 돋우기 위해 박자 와 라임을 넣은 말을 했다는 설명 뒤에 그들이 디제잉과 리듬 감 있는 외침을 동시에 할 수가 없었을 때의 상황이 제시되었 고, 빈칸 뒤에서는 that is(즉)로 사회자 곧 엠씨가 언급되므로, 친구에게 자신을 대신해 관중에게 말을 하는 진행자의 역할을 부탁했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❹ ‘청중에 게 말하는 것’이 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

Nobody knows the exact origin, but (A)it is said

party, reminded him in a jokey way (C)that his days
of freedom were over by moving across the stage
like a military instructor to the beat, chanting,

don’t stop.” Such lines became a standard part of
rap and were included in the lyrics of the first
recorded hip-hop album, Rapper’s Delight (1979),
which was an immediate success.
The new music and dancing spread very fast.
There was a sharp unexplained decline in violence
during the 1980s in New York. One police officer
asked a boy on the street (E)if he knew why. The
boy said, “It’s because they’re dancing.”

body:
A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a psychology professor at Cornell University,
reached a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t
spend your money on things. We assume that the
happiness we get from buying something will last
as long as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The
trouble with things is that the happiness they
provide fades quickly. There are three critical
reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. What once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep raising the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
get used to a new possession, we look for an even
better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans to
compare themselves with others. We buy a new car
and are thrilled with it until a friend buys a better
one, and there’s always someone with a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we
are the accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we’ve been to.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves
than our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can really
like your material stuff. You can even think that
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain separate from you. On
the other hand, your experiences really are part of
you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

body:
A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a psychology professor at Cornell University,
reached a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t
spend your money on things. We assume that the
happiness we get from buying something will last
as long as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The
trouble with things is that the happiness they
provide fades quickly. There are three critical
reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. What once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep raising the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
get used to a new possession, we look for an even
better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans to
compare themselves with others. We buy a new car
and are thrilled with it until a friend buys a better
one, and there’s always someone with a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we
are the accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we’ve been to.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves
than our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can really
like your material stuff. You can even think that
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain separate from you. On
the other hand, your experiences really are part of
you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The assumption that owning things can sustainhappiness is misguided.
We soon grow accustomed to new possessions,so the happiness they provide fades quickly.
Raising our standards and comparing ourselveswith others fail to bring lasting happiness.
Gilovich and other researchers have revealedthat experiences are a source of happiness.
Experiences and material possessions can contributeequally to shaping personal identity.

Most people use their cell phone everywhere. But research shows that cell phones are far dirtier than most people think, and the more germs they collect, the more germs you touch. In fact, our hands are to blame. Americans check their phones about 47 times a day, and this spreads germs from hands to the phone. A recent study found more than 17,000 bacterial gene copies on the phones of high school students. Scientists at the University of Arizona have found that cell phones carry 10 times more bacteria than most toilet seats. While most germs on phones aren't harmful, some can be. One of the worst places to use your phone is in the bathroom. When toilets flush, they spread bad germs everywhere. Keeping your phone out of the bathroom will help. You can wipe it with a soft towel, which will remove many of the germs. For a deeper clean, use a mix of 60% water and 40% alcohol. Still, the best advice has more to do with you than the phone. Wash your hands several times a day, and you'll likely be fine.

It appears that viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated to have killed 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, affecting almost every aspect of human life worldwide.
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter human bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in ______, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: more frequent contact between humans and wild animals
a decrease in the number of wild animals living near humans
stronger natural barriers separating humans from wild animal habitats
an increase in the spread of viruses among different animal species
fewer opportunities for viruses to enter human bodies without immunity

solution: 지구에 산소를 공급하는 바이러스의 역할과 관련해, 바이러스가 박테리아를 감염시켜 죽이지 않는다면 죽은 박테리아에서 나온 영양소를 주 먹이로 하는 플랑크톤이 부족해지고, 지구 산소의 약 절반을 생산하는 플랑크톤이 부족하면 산소가 부족해져 인류의 생존이 불가능할 것이라고 설명하는 흐름이므로, 플랑크톤의 감소가 해양 생물 개체 수에 미치는 영향에 대한 내용인 (D) ‘플랑크톤은 작은 해양 생물부터 물고기와 고래에 이르기까지 많은 생물의 먹이가 되므로, 플랑크톤 감소는 해양 생물의 개체 수 감소로 이어질 수 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 무관하다.

body:
(A)[That / What] is less commonly known is that viruses play crucial roles in supporting much of life on Earth. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses that ⓐsustain us and the planet, instead of just those (B)[who / which] harm us. Therefore, scientists have much more to learn about viruses than they currently know. What they do know is (C)[that / which] viruses act as the primary ⓑfacilitators of bacterial and insect populations.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, they ⓒaid the reproductive functions of other organisms to multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses go on to ⓓinfect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses ⓔcontrol the excessive growth of certain bacteria.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: What which that
That who which
What which which
What who that
That who that
solution:
(A) 불완전한 절 ‘is less commonly known’을 이끌어 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 What이 알맞다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절 ‘harm us’를 이끌어 those를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 주격 관계대명사 자리이며, 선행사 those가 the viruses를 가리키므로, 사물 선행사와 쓰이는 which가 알맞다.
(C) is의 보어 자리에서 완전한 절 ‘viruses act ~ insect populations’를 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.

body:
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution is their role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ that helps the fetus grow securely inside its mother’s body. It facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while protecting the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, making them vulnerable to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to carry their young inside their bodies safely from one location to another. Viruses that infected our remote ancestors more than 130 million years ago have been reported to have served a key function in the development of this vital organ.
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Placenta as a Defense Against Viral Infections
Viruses as a Major Threat to Mammalian Reproduction
The Evolutionary Benefits of Carrying Young Inside the Body
Ancient Viruses and the Spread of Diseases Among Mammals
How Viruses Helped Mammals Evolve a Safer Way to Carry Their Young

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is ⓐthat they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients ⓑreleasing from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses ⓒdid not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans ⓓsurvive.
Insect species populations ⓔare also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses ⓕthat infect those insects also increase, reducing their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects ⓖto flourish. (A)자연의 먹이사슬을 고려할 때, 바이러스가 다른 종을 조절하는 중요한 기능을 수행한다고 가정하는 것은 어렵지 않을 것이다. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓑ releasing → released (is의 보어인 명사 nutrients를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 수 있으나, 수식받는 명사가 타동사 release(~을 방출하다)의 주체가 아니라 대상이고, 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 releasing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 released로 고친다.)
ⓓ survive → to survive (make 뒤에 가목적어 it과 목적격보어인 형용사 impossible이 쓰였으며, to부정사의 의미상 주어로 쓰이는 ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 for humans가 이어졌으므로, ‘make+가목적어(it)+목적격보어+진목적어(for+목적격+to부정사)(-가 ~하는 것을 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구조를 이루는 to부정사를 써야 한다. 따라서 동사 survive를 to부정사인 to survive로 고친다.)

body:
As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing them in the battle against diseases are arising. Of notable interest ⓐare the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment. Genes can be compared to instruction guides that govern how our bodies function. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, which can lead to health problems. Gene therapy steps in ⓑto fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering corrected genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, ⓒenables them to function properly. In this process, specially modified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, it can potentially help the body fight off certain diseases.
ⓓUsing viruses to treat cancer, another use of viruses, is based on the notion of utilizing their natural ability to infect and kill cells. If successful, viruses can be manipulated to specifically target and ⓔdestroying cancer cells while leaving healthy cells unharmed. The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment is still in the early stages. However, many researchers are involved in hundreds of projects with the goal of discovering cures for diseases that ⓕonce thought to be incurable.
We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. (A)하지만 바이러스에 대해 더 많이 알수록 특정 바이러스를 유익한 목적으로 사용하고 다음 팬데믹으로 이어질 수 있는 바이러스에 대한 방어책을 개발하는 데 더 잘 대비할 수 있을 것이다. More than that, learning more about viral diversity will help us ⓖreach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓒ enables → enabling (동사(lies)가 있는 완전한 절(The essence of ~ cells)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 뒤에 목적어 them과 목적격보어인 to부정사구가 이어져 ‘enable+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …하는 것을 가능하게 하다)’의 능동태 5형식을 이루므로, enables를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 enabling으로 고친다.)
ⓔ destroying → destroy (to와 부사 specifically에 이어진 동사원형 target과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 목적(~하기 위해서)을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사구를 이루어야 하므로, destroying을 동사원형 destroy로 고친다.)
ⓕ once thought → were once thought (주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절의 동사 자리에 흐름상 과거시제가 쓰인 것과 동사 앞에 ‘한때’라는 의미의 부사로 once가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 선행사 diseases가 과거 ‘여겨졌던’ 대상이고, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’think+목적어+(to be+)보어(~을 …라고 생각하다)‘의 to부정사 to be와 보어 incurable이 이어져 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ’be thought+(to be+)보어(…라고 생각되다)‘를 이루어야 한다. 따라서 복수명사인 선행사에 수일치한 과거형 be동사 were를 사용하고, 부사는 보통 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 위치하므로, once thought를 were once thought로 고친다.)

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. (A) They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick. (B)
But they were wrong. (C) The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. (D) The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague. (E)
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘흑사병은 동물에서 사람으로 퍼질 수 있는 박테리아에 의해 발생했다.’라는 뜻으로, 흑사병의 실제 원인을 설명하고 있으므로, 흑사병의 원인에 대한 당시 의사들의 믿음과 그들이 사용한 방법을 기술하고 나서 그들이 틀렸음을 밝힌 뒤이자, also(또한)을 사용해 박테리아가 벼룩에 물리거나 아픈 사람과의 접촉을 통해서도 퍼질 수 있었다는 또 다른 확산의 원인을 추가 설명하는 문장 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. (A) They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick. (B)
But they were wrong. (C) The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. (D) The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague. (E)
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
윗글의 내용을 제대로 이해하지 못한 사람은?
Jisu: Doctors who treated the plague at that time used sticks to touch infected patients.
Hojun: They believed that bad air caused the plague by disturbing the balance inside the body.
Taeju: They also filled the masks they wore with herbs that were believed to filter the air.
Jiyeon: Doctors at that time seemed to have little understanding of the cause of the plague or how to treat it.
Eunji: Even today, it is still difficult to detect and respond to bacteria and viruses.

solution: 현대 의학 덕분에 우리는 박테리아와 바이러스를 신속하게 탐지하고 대응할 수 있게 되었다고 했으므로, ‘오늘날에도 박테리아와 바이러스를 탐지하고 대응하는 것은 여전히 어려워.’라고 말한 은지가 글의 내용을 제대로 이해하지 못한 사람이다.

We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. The more we learn about viruses, however, the better equipped we will be to use certain viruses for beneficial purposes and to develop defenses against viruses that could lead to the next pandemic. More than that, learning more about viral diversity will help us reach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.

body:
G: Dad, I’ve been thinking about participating in the underwater cleanup program.
M: Really? How does that program actually work?

(A) Don’t worry. They offer different roles based on swimming and diving experience, so anyone can participate.
(B) Hmm, but I’m worried you don’t have much experience in underwater activities.
(C) You’re right, Dad. I’ll make sure to do more research before participating in the program.
(D) Well, participants head out into the sea and gather underwater waste.
(E) I see. It’s good to be involved in a good cause, but I think you should learn more about the program before you participate. Safety should always come first.

다음 주어진 대화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 수중 정화 프로그램에 참여할까 생각중이라는 딸의 말에 아버지가 그 프로그램이 실제로 어떻게 진행되는지를 묻는 주어진 대화에 이어, 프로그램 진행 방식에 대해 참가자들이 바다로 나가 수중 쓰레기를 수거한다고 설명하는 (D), 딸이 수중 활동 경험이 많지 않다는 점을 걱정하며 안전에 대한 우려를 나타내는 (B), 수영과 다이빙 경험에 따라 참가자들에게 서로 다른 역할이 주어지므로 누구나 참여할 수 있다고 설명하며 걱정하지 말라고 아빠를 안심시키는 (A), 딸의 설명에 ‘I see.(그렇구나.)’라며 수긍한 뒤 참여하기 전에 프로그램에 대해 더 알아보고 안전을 최우선시하라고 한 번 더 조언하는 (E), 아빠의 조언에 ‘You’re right, Dad.(맞아요, 아빠.)‘라고 말하며 동의한 뒤 참여 전에 프로그램에 대해 꼭 더 조사해보겠다고 말하는 (C)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, ⓐincreases its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in (A)capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes ⓑhave been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times (B)more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and ⓒstored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that ⓓhas dissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, (C)accelerating global warming.
Nevertheless, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet saving function ⓔdepending on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and ⓕaid in the planet’s decarbonization. Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, rethinking industrial fishing practices, (D)restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution ⓖentered the sea. By (E)prioritizing ocean health, we can unlock its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.

choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
ⓐ increases → increasing
ⓔ depending → depends
ⓖ entered → entering

Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to ______. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean’s conservation.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: strengthening marine law enforcement
monitoring changes in marine environments
prioritizing ocean research and conservation
strengthening cooperation with marine scientists
advancing technological innovation in marine industries
solution: Earle의 노력에도 불구하고 그녀는 정부 고위 관리로서 표현과 행동의 자유에 대한 제약에 직면해 보다 적극적인 환경 운동가가 되고자 2년 후 미국 국립해양대기청(NOAA)에서 사임했고, 민간 부문에서 해양 보호 캠페인을 위해 자신의 전문 지식과 경험을 활용했다고 설명하고 있으므로, NOAA의 첫 여성 과학자가 된 후 해양 자원 개발에서 해양의 연구와 보호로 NOAA의 초점을 바꾸고자 노력했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❸ ‘해양 연구와 보전에 우선순위를 두는 것’이 알맞다.

body:
When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there?” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life ⓐwhich I see.” Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.
Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. ⓑHaving moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is ⓒdive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake ⓓworn the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle (A)______. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine ⓔscientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: was relieved to return safely to the surface
was surprised to find the water extremely cold
was curious to discover what lay beyond the familiar shoreline
was concerned to notice the limited visibility below the surface
was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire ⓐto explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats ⓑsituated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge just couldn’t cope with the idea ⓒthat men and women living together underwater,” she said. The following year, ⓓhave chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks ⓔliving 15 meters beneath the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes.
Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and ⓕunderstood the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings ⓖwere published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, ⓗreceived attention similar to that of the astronauts’ historic moon landing.

body:
For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the importance of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.”
With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and preserve the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.

Earle’s contributions to marine science and her lifelong efforts to raise awareness of the ⓐ______ of the ocean and the need for its conservation continue to inspire future generations to ⓑ______ the blue heart of our planet.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ
choices: value pioneer
immensity develop
significance safeguard
beauty explore
vastness research
solution: [요약문] Earle의 해양 과학 분야에 대한 기여와 바다의 ⓐ중요성 및 바다 보전의 필요성에 대한 인식을 높이려는 평생의 노력은 미래 세대가 우리 행성의 푸른 심장을 ⓑ보호하도록 계속해서 영감을 준다.

body:
In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and ⓐwalking on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” (A) As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. (B) Among them were some species she had studied but ⓑnever seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend ⓒit. (C) She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. (D) The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet ⓓto explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” (E) Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day ⓔwhen human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘잠수하는 동안, Earle은 우주 탐험과 비교하여 해양 탐험의 중요성을 상징하기 위해 해저에 깃발을 꽂았다.’라는 뜻으로, 해저에 다다른 이후의 상황을 설명하고 있으므로, Earle이 당시 세계에서 가장 깊은 단독 다이빙을 했으며 바닷속으로 내려가면서 본 생물들에 매료되었다는 내용 뒤이자, 주어진 문장에 언급된 해저에 깃발을 꽂은 순간을 the moment(그 순간)로 가리켜, Earle이 그 순간을 Neil Armstrong이 달에 첫발을 내디딘 순간과 연관시켰다고 설명하는 문장 앞인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support.
Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for maintaining ocean health.

Earle devoted her life to ______ ______ ______ of the ocean’s significance, and her efforts came to prominence through the launch of ______ ______ ______ ______, her receipt of the TED Prize, and the establishment of ______ ______ to encourage efforts to explore and protect the ocean.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것)
answer: raising public awareness / a global digital platform / Mission Blue
solution: [요약문] Earle은 바다의 중요성에 대한 대중의 인식을 높이는 것에 자신의 삶을 바쳤으며, 그녀의 노력은 글로벌 디지털 플랫폼의 시작, TED 상 수상, 그리고 바다를 탐험하고 보호하기 위한 노력을 장려하기 위한 미션 블루의 설립을 통해 알려졌다.

body:
For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, (A)멸종 위기에 처한 해양 생물을 보호할 희망이 있다. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the importance of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.”
With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and preserve the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.

Earle mentioned that roughly half of the world’s coral reefs and 90% of its sharks have disappeared since the 1980s.
Earle pointed out that humans lack the capacity to bear responsibility for the harm inflicted on the ocean.
Earle underscores the significance of the ocean, saying, “No ocean, no life.”
Sylvia Earle has left a significant mark on marine science through countless hours of underwater experiences and numerous explorations.
solution: Earle은 바다에 가해지는 많은 스트레스에 대한 인간의 책임이 크지만, 우리에게 바다의 생존을 보장할 수 있는 힘도 있다고 믿는다고 언급하고 있으므로, ❸ ‘Earle은 인간이 바다에 가해지는 피해에 대해 책임을 질 능력이 부족하다고 지적했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began to explore the beaches and ⓐ[observe / observing] the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
(A)17세에, 그녀는 친구 아버지가 입던 잠수복을 입고 호수에서 10미터 아래로 내려가 그녀의 첫 심해 다이빙을 했다. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore ⓑ[growing / grew], and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her ⓒ[to become / becoming] a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: observing growing to become
observe growing becoming
observe grew to become
observing grew to become
observe grew becoming
solution:
ⓐ began의 목적어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to explore와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, to가 생략된 동사원형 observe가 알맞다.
ⓑ 명사구 her desire를 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to explore가 수식해 ‘탐험하려는 그녀의 열망’이라는 뜻의 주어부를 이룬 her desire to explore에 대한 동사가 올 자리이므로, 자동사 grow의 과거형인 grew가 알맞다.

body:
When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there?” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see.” Long before others, this person recognized that not only ⓐthe ocean is full of life, but that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.
Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and ⓑobserving the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is ⓒdived in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
At 17, she took her first deep dive, ⓓdescended 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle was thrilled ⓔto observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become (A)______.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a skilled diver and instructor
a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation
a researcher specializing in predicting changes in ocean currents
a leading scientist devoted to designing advanced diving equipment
an environmentalist who led efforts to protect coastal waters from illegal activities
solution: Sylvia Earle은 다른 사람들보다 훨씬 먼저 바다의 매력을 알아보고 바다가 생명으로 가득할 뿐 아니라 보호해야 할 대상이라는 사실을 깨달은 전설적인 해양 생물학자로서, 어린 시절 다이빙의 짜릿함을 경험하면서 스쿠버 장비를 사용한 최초의 해양 과학자 중 한 명이 되었다고 했으므로, 그녀의 타고난 모험심과 호기심이 학문적 여정을 이끌었다는 내용 뒤에 해양을 탐구하고 보호하는 데 있어 선두적인 인물이 되었다는 결과가 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❷ ‘해양 탐험과 보전의 선구자’가 알맞다.

body:
Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge just couldn’t cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater,” she said. (A)이듬해, 그녀는 전부 여성으로 구성된 텍타이트 II 프로젝트를 이끌도록 선정되어, 다른 해양학자 네 명과 함께 해저 15미터에서 생활하며 2주를 보냈다. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes.
Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts’ historic moon landing.

As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species. There are (B)[more / less] whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the (C)[importance / danger] of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.”

(A) (B) (C)

development less danger

solution:
(A) Earle이 해양학자이자 작가, 강연가로서 사람들이 해양의 중요성을 인식하도록 지속적으로 영감을 주고 있다는 설명이 이어지므로, 미션 블루가 바다에 대한 열정 및 바다 보존에 대한 헌신을 바탕으로 하는 운동이라는 흐름이 되는 preservation(보존)이 알맞다.

body:
In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Sylvia Earle’s pioneering contributions to the development of underwater exploration technology
the growing reputation of Sylvia Earle as a prominent figure in ocean conservation
Sylvia Earle’s unprecedented deep-sea expedition and its symbolic significance
what inspired Sylvia Earle to challenge the limits of human exploration
Sylvia Earle’s future plans for unexplored regions of space and the ocean
solution: 1979년 Sylvia Earle은 당시 세계에서 가장 깊은 것으로 기록된 단독 다이빙을 통해 그동안 연구하면서 한 번도 본 적이 없는 종들을 포함한 바다 생물들을 관찰했고, 잠수하는 동안 해저에 깃발을 꽂아 우주 탐험에 필적하는 해양 탐험의 중요성을 보여주었으며, 이러한 그녀의 업적은 인류가 바닷속의 광활한 생명 세계를 알고 존중하게 될 날을 향한 작은 발걸음이었다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ❸ ‘Sylvia Earle의 전례 없는 심해 탐험과 그것의 상징적 의미’가 알맞다.

body:
Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean’s conservation.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 지문에서 찾아 알맞게 쓰시오. (각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것)
As NOAA’s first female chief scientist, Earle sought to shift its focus toward ______ ______ ______ ______, but resigned due to restricted freedom of expression, continuing her efforts in the ______ ______ to protect the oceans using her ______ ______ ______.
answer: As NOAA’s first female chief scientist, Earle sought to shift its focus toward ocean research and conservation, but resigned due to restricted freedom of expression, continuing her efforts in the private sector to protect the oceans using her expertise and experience.
solution: [요약문] NOAA의 첫 여성 수석 과학자로서, Earle은 그것의 초점을 해양 연구와 보전으로 전환하고자 했지만 제한된 표현의 자유로 인해 사임했으며, 자신의 전문 지식과 경험을 활용해 민간 부문에서 해양을 보호하기 위한 노력을 계속했다.

body:
Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. (A)그녀는 글로벌 디지털 플랫폼을 시작하는 데 중요한 역할을 했는데, 이는 사용자가 가상으로 수중 세계를 탐험하며 해양 생태계에 대한 이해를 높이도록 하는 것이었다. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support.
Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for maintaining ocean health.

윗글의 두 번째 단락의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to describe the effects of “Hope Spots” on the recovery of endangered marine species
to explain the principles underlying Mission Blue and its approach to ocean conservation
to discuss the challenges of establishing effective systems for protecting marine ecosystems

(A)______, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. ⓐCovered 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes ⓑhave found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon ⓒis commonly knowing as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide ⓓthat has dissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming.
(B)______, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet saving function ⓔdepends on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and aid in the planet’s decarbonization. Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, rethinking industrial fishing practices, restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and ⓕreduce pollution entering the sea. By prioritizing ocean health, we can unlock its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.

(B) 해양은 육지보다 16배 많은 탄소를 보유하고 있으며, 해양에 저장된 블루카본이 지구 온난화를 방지한다는 순기능에 대한 설명 뒤에, 지구 보호 기능을 수행하는 해양의 능력은 해양의 건강에 달려 있다는 문제를 언급하므로, '그럼에도 불구하고‘라는 뜻으로 역접을 나타내는 Nevertheless 또는 Nonetheless가 알맞다.

solution:
ⓐ Covered → Covering
(콤마(,) 뒤에 완전한 절(the ocean plays ~ the atmosphere)이 접속사 없이 이어지므로, 콤마(,) 앞은 주절 앞에 쓰여 흐름상 주절 주어를 부연 설명하는 분사구문의 형태가 되어야 한다. 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상의 주어 the ocean이 ‘차지하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 70% of Earth가 이어지므로, Covered를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Covering으로 고친다.)
ⓑ have found → have been found
(부사구 For thousands of years와 함께 과거부터 현재까지 수천 년 동안 ‘밝혀져 왔다’는 의미를 나타내기 위해 핵심주어인 복수명사구 marine ecosystems에 수일치한 복수 조동사(have)를 사용해 현재완료가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주어가 ‘밝혀진’ 대상이고, 뒤에 수동 표현인 ‘be found+to부정사(~라는 것이 밝혀지다)’의 to부정사가 이어져 있으므로, 현재완료 능동태(have[has]+p.p.)가 아닌 현재완료 수동태(have[has] +been+p.p.)를 사용해 have found를 have been found 로 고친다.)
ⓒ is commonly knowing → is commonly known
(주어 This captured carbon이 단수명사구이므로 단수동사로 수일치하는 것과 be동사와 분사 사이에 부사 commonly가 위치한 것은 모두 알맞으나, 주어가 “blue carbon”으로 ‘알려진’ 대상이며, 뒤에 ‘know ~ as …(~을 …로 알다)’의 목적어 없이 전치사 as와 명사구 “blue carbon”이 바로 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘~ be known as …(~가 …로 알려지다)’를 사용해 is commonly knowing을 is commonly known으로 고친다.)
ⓕ reduce → reducing
(타동사 include(~을 포함하다)의 목적어 자리에 쓰인 동명사 protecting, rethinking, restoring과 ’A, B, C and D’ 구조로 병렬 연결되며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사 pollution이 있으므로, reduce를 능동형 동명사 reducing으로 고친다.)

Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean.
(A) At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater.
(B) Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.
(C) As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: Sylvia Earle의 플로리다에서의 첫 생일에 부모님이 바다를 사랑하는 그녀에게 딱 맞는 물안경을 선물했다는 내용에 이어, 물안경을 These로 가리켜 아버지가 ‘이것들’이 수중 탐험에 도움이 될 것이라고 말하며 잠수를 격려했다는 내용의 (B), 17세에 Earle이 친구 아버지가 입던 잠수복을 입고 첫 심해 다이빙을 했고, 물고기를 관찰할 수 있다는 사실에 감격했다는 내용의 (A), 다이빙의 짜릿함을 경험하면서 그녀의 탐험에 대한 열망이 커져 학문적 여정을 이어갔고, 스쿠버 장비를 사용한 최초의 해양 과학자 중 한 명으로서 해양 탐험과 보전의 선구자가 되었다는 내용의 (C)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

However, there is hope ⓑ[of / that] preserving endangered marine species. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the importance of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, ⓒ[imagine / imaging] Earth without it. No ocean, no life.”

ⓐ ‘inspire+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하도록 고무[자극]하다)’의 5형식 구문에 쓰일 때 inspire는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, 동사 inspires와 목적어 individuals에 이어진 목적격보어 자리에 to부정사인 to acknowledge가 알맞다.

(B) 유전자 치료와 암 치료에 바이러스를 사용하는 것은 아직 초기 단계에 머물러 있다는 내용이 앞서 언급되었으므로, 많은 연구자들이 한때 불치병으로 여겨졌던 질병의 치료법을 발견하기 위해 연구하고 있다는 흐름이 되는 incurable(치료 불가능한, 불치의)이 알맞다.
curable 치료 가능한
(C) 바이러스에 대해 더 많이 알게 될수록 가능한 결과로서, 다음 팬데믹으로 이어질 수 있는 바이러스에 대한 방어책을 개발하는 데 더 잘 대비할 수 있을 것이라는 흐름이 되는 lead to(~로 이어지다)가 알맞다.
ward ~ off ~을 막다[피하다]

body:
It appears that viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated ⓐto kill 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, affecting almost every aspect of human life worldwide.
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses ⓑentering human bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests ⓒpreventing animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, ⓓmeant more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern ⓔwhich pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지 못한 것은?
choices: ⓐ to kill → to have killed
ⓑ entering → to enter
ⓒ preventing → prevented
ⓓ meant → meaning
ⓔ which → what
solution:
ⓔ which → that (추상명사 concern(걱정, 우려)의 구체적 내용을 나타내는 완전한 절(pandemics may increase in the future)을 연결하고 있으므로, which를 what이 아닌 동격 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘~한 것으로 추정되다’라는 뜻의 ‘be estimated+to부정사(구)’에서 추정되는 시점이 현재이므로 현재시제 is estimated가 쓰였으나 사람들이 사망한 것은 과거의 일이며, to부정사(구)의 내용이 본동사의 시제보다 이전 상황이면 완료부정사(to have p.p.)를 사용하므로, to kill을 to have killed로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …하게 하다)’의 5형식에서 allow의 목적격보어로 to부정사(구)가 쓰이므로 entering을 to enter로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓒ 주어 natural barriers such as mountains and forests에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 흐름상 과거의 일을 나타내야 하고, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 animal viruses가 있으므로, preventing을 과거시제 능동태인 prevented로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓓ 앞의 완전한 절(These changes ~ wild animals)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사구가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절을 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 ‘의미하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 완전한 절 형태의 명사절이 이어져 있으므로, meant를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 meaning으로 고친 것은 알맞다.

body:
Another less recognized role of viruses is their contribution to the evolution of life on Earth. When a virus infects a reproductive cell of its host, such as an egg or sperm, the viral DNA may be passed down to the host’s offspring. The insertion of new DNA into genomes is a significant mechanism of evolution. Without viruses, in other words, the evolutionary potential for all life on the planet would be impacted.
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Evolution of Virus Throughout Human History
The Significant Impact of Viruses on the Evolution of Life on Earth
The Damage Viruses Cause to the Genomes of Living Organisms
The Contributions of Viruses to the Spread of Infectious Diseases
The Process of Viral DNA Transmission from Parents to Their Offspring

body:
(A)덜 일반적으로 알려진 것은 바이러스들이 지구상의 많은 생명체를 지탱하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 것이다. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses that sustain us and the planet, instead of just those that harm us. Therefore, scientists have much more to learn about viruses than they currently know. What they do know is that viruses act as the primary regulators of bacterial and insect populations.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, (B)they steal the reproductive functions of other organisms to multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses go on to infect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses control the excessive growth of certain bacteria.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)they steal the reproductive functions of other organisms가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Viruses protect host cells from harmful substances.
Viruses destroy host cells to prevent them from reproducing.
Viruses change host cells to make them resistant to other viruses.
Viruses provide host cells with the materials they need to reproduce.
Viruses take advantage of host cells to make copies of themselves.
solution:

오답
① 바이러스는 숙주 세포를 해로운 물질들로부터 보호한다.
② 바이러스는 숙주 세포가 번식하지 못하도록 그것을 파괴한다.
③ 바이러스는 숙주 세포가 다른 바이러스에 저항력을 갖도록 만들기 위해 그것을 변화시킨다.
④ 바이러스는 숙주 세포에게 번식하는 데 필요한 물질들을 제공한다.

As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing them in the battle against diseases are ⓐarising. Of notable interest are the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment. Genes can be compared to instruction guides that ⓑgovern how our bodies function. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, which can lead to health problems. Gene therapy steps in to fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering ⓒwrong genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, enabling them to function properly. In this process, specially ⓓmodified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, it can potentially help the body ⓔfight off certain diseases.

body:
The greater significance of viruses ⓐinfected bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth ⓑis produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses ⓒdid not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, (A)바이러스들이 없다면, 산소의 부족이 인류가 생존하는 것을 불가능하게 만들 것이다.
Insect species populations are also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses that infect those insects also increase, ⓓreduced their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects ⓔflourish. Considering the chain of food in nature, it would not be difficult ⓕto assume that viruses fulfill important functions in regulating other species. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ infected →infecting (전치사 of의 목적어인 명사 viruses를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사 자리이며, 수식받는 명사가 ‘감염시키는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사 bacteria가 있으므로, infected를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 infecting으로 고친다.)
ⓓ reduced → reducing (완전한 절(the viruses ~ increase) 뒤에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이끄는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 ‘줄이는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 their numbers가 있으므로, reduce를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 reducing으로 고친다.)
ⓔ flourish → to flourish (앞에 to부정사의 의미상 주어로 쓰이는 ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 for other types of insects가 있으며, 흐름상 명사 room을 ‘다른 종류의 곤충들이 번성할 (여지)’라는 뜻으로 수식하는 형용사구를 이루어야 하므로, 동사 flourish를 to부정사인 to flourish로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 주절에 조동사 과거형 would와 동사원형 be가 쓰였으며, 주절과 조건절이 모두 현재 사실의 반대를 가정해야 하므로, ‘If+S+과거동사 ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …(만약 ~한다면, …할 텐데[…할 것이다])’ 형태의 가정법 과거를 사용해 If절에 과거형 조동사 did와 부정어 not이 쓰여 동사구 infect and kill의 부정형을 이룬 것은 알맞다.

body:
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution (A)[is / are] ⓐtheir role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ that helps the fetus (B)[grow / growing] securely inside ⓑits mother’s body. ⓒIt facilitates the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while protecting the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, making ⓓthem vulnerable to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to carry their young inside ⓔtheir bodies safely from one location to another. Viruses that infected our remote ancestors more than 130 million years ago have been reported (C)[to serve / to have served] a key function in the development of this vital organ.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: is / grow / to serve
is / grow / to have served
are / grow / to have served
are / growing / to serve
is / growing / to have served
solution:
(A) 주어 One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution의 핵심단어가 단수명사 example이므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 알맞다.
(B) ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식 구문에서 준사역동사 help의 목적격보어로 to부정사나 동사원형이 쓰이므로, 동사원형 grow가 알맞다.
(C) ‘be reported+to부정사(~한 것으로 보고되다, ~라고 한다)’의 to부정사가 올 자리이며, 주어 Viruses가 ‘역할을 했던’ 것이 보고된 상태(have been reported)인 현재시점보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로, 완료부정사(to have p.p.)인 to have served가 알맞다.

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
But they were wrong. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
But they were wrong. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
