In 1918, as "World WarⅠ" was ending, a very deadly flu called the "Spanish Flu" spread around the world. It infected many people, causing the deaths of around 50 million, even more than the number of people who died in the war.

(B) The flu reached places like the United States, Europe, and even remote areas like Greenland and the Pacific islands. Some people thought it was called the Spanish Flu because it started in Spain, but that's not true.
(C) Spain was the only country hit by the virus that was not involved in "World WarⅠ." Therefore it was the only country to report the true extent of the pandemic.

(D) These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. 어법상 알맞은 것은 총 4개이다.
ⓒ 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사를 남겨 둔 ‘접속사+분사(구)’ 형태의 분사구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어인 healthy cells와 목적격보어인 형용사 unharmed가 이어져 ‘leave+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)(~을 …한 상태로 남겨두다)’의 능동태 5형식 구문을 이루므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 leaving은 알맞다.
ⓓ 주어 The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment의 핵심단어가 단수명사 use이므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is는 알맞다.
ⓕ ’the+비교급‘이 쓰인 앞 절(The more ~ viruses)에 상응해 ’the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 …(~ 할수록, 더 …하다)‘을 이루어야 하며, 주어 we가 ’equip+목적어+to부정사(~에게 …할 능력[기술]을 키워주다)‘의 동사 equip의 대상이므로, ’the+비교급‘인 the better 뒤에 수동 표현인 ’be equipped+to부정사‘의 equipped가 쓰인 the better equipped는 알맞다.
ⓖ ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식 구문에서 준사역동사 help의 목적격보어로 to부정사나 동사원형이 쓰이며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 a deeper understanding이 이어져 있으므로, help와 목적어 us 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 타동사 reach(~에 이르다)가 능동태 동사원형으로 쓰인 것은 알맞다.
오답
ⓐ are → is (주어인 동명사구 Using viruses to treat cancer와 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입된 동격 어구 another use of viruses 뒤에 문장의 동사로 ’be based on ~(~에 근거하다, ~에 기반을 두다)‘의 be동사가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 동명사(구) 주어는 단수 취급하므로 수일치를 위해 복수동사 are를 단수동사 is로 고친다.)
ⓑ successfully → successful (부사절 접속사 If 뒤에 ’주어+be동사‘인 it is가 생략되었으므로 생략된 be동사(is)의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 올 자리이다. 보어 자리에 부사는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사 successfully를 형용사 successful로 고친다.)
ⓔ being incurable → to be incurable (’~을 …라고 생각하다‘라는 뜻의 ’think+목적어+(to be+)보어‘의 수동 표현인 ’be thought+(to be+)보어(…라고 생각되다)‘를 이루어야 하므로, being incurable을 to be incurable로 고친다.)

body:
Using viruses to treat cancer, another use of viruses, ⓐare based on the notion of utilizing their natural ability to infect and kill cells. If ⓑsuccessfully, viruses can be manipulated to specifically target and destroy cancer cells while ⓒleaving healthy cells unharmed. The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment ⓓis still in the early stages. (A)______, many researchers are involved in hundreds of projects with the goal of discovering cures for diseases that were once thought ⓔbeing incurable.
We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. The more we learn about viruses, however, ⓕthe better equipped we will be to use certain viruses for beneficial purposes and to develop defenses against viruses that could lead to the next pandemic. (B)______, learning more about viral diversity will help us ⓖreach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.
윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: However / What’s more
Namely / Unfortunately
Nevertheless / In contrast
That is to say / Conversely
For example / More than that
solution:
(A) 유전자 치료와 암 치료에 바이러스를 사용하는 것은 아직 초기 단계에 머물러 있다는 내용 뒤에 많은 연구자들이 치료법을 발견하기 위해 수백 개의 프로젝트에 참여하고 있다는 대조적인 내용이 이어지므로, 역접을 나타내는 However(그러나) 또는 Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)가 알맞다.
(B) 바이러스에 대해 더 많이 알게 되는 것은 특정 바이러스를 유익한 목적으로 사용하고 다음 팬데믹으로 이어질 수 있는 바이러스에 대한 방어책을 개발하는 데 더 잘 대비할 수 있게 한다는 이점 뒤에, 지구와 생태계, 우리 몸의 작용에 대해 더 깊이 이해할 수 있도록 도움을 준다는 또 다른 이점을 추가하므로, What’s more(게다가) 또는 More than that(그 이상으로, 뿐만 아니라)이 알맞다.
*원래 지문에는 More than that이 쓰였음
오답
② 즉, 다시 말해서 / 불행히도, 유감스럽게도
③ 그럼에도 불구하고 / 대조적으로
④ 즉, 다시 말해서 / 반대로, 역으로
⑤ 예를 들어 / 그 이상으로, 뿐만 아니라

body:
ⓐIt appears that viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. ⓑThe 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated to have killed 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, ⓒaffecting almost every aspect of human life worldwide.
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter ⓓhuman bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, ⓔmeaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: Viruses appear to exist solely to bring suffering to humanity.
ⓑ: It is estimated that the 1918 influenza pandemic kills 50 to 100 million people.
ⓒ: and it affects almost every aspect of human life worldwide
ⓓ: human bodies which have no prior immunity to such viruses
ⓔ: which means more opportunities for the viruses that are present in wild animals to spread to humans
solution:
ⓑ ‘be estimated+to부정사(구)(~할 것으로 추정되다)’는 가주어 It과 진주어인 that절을 사용해 ‘It+be estimated+that절’ 구조로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으나, is estimated 뒤에 추정되는 시점보다 이전의 과거에 발생한 일을 나타내는 완료부정사(to have killed)가 쓰였으므로 진주어인 that절에 현재시제 kills가 아닌 과거시제 killed를 사용해야 한다. 따라서 ‘It is estimated that the 1918 influenza pandemic killed 50 to 100 million people.’로 전환해야 한다.
오답
ⓐ ‘~한 것처럼 보인다’라는 뜻의 가주어-진주어 구문인 ‘It appears+that절’은 that절의 주어를 주절 주어 자리로 이동시켜 ’주어+appear+to부정사(구)‘로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으므로, that 뒤의 viruses를 주절 주어로 하고, 복수명사인 주어에 수일치 시켜 복수동사 appear를 쓴 뒤, 동사 exist를 to부정사로 바꿔 ’Viruses appear to exist solely to bring suffering to humanity.‘로 전환한 것은 알맞다.
ⓒ 앞의 완전한 절(the recent ~ lives)에 콤마(,)로 이어져 흐름상 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문이므로 접속사 and를 사용해 ’and+대명사(주어)+동사~‘로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 주절 주어인 단수명사구 the recent COVID-19 pandemic과 동일하므로 and 뒤에 이를 가리키는 단수대명사 it을 사용하고, 분사구문의 내용이 현재의 일반적 사실에 해당하므로 현재시제이자 it에 수일치한 단수동사 affects를 써서 ’and it affects almost every aspect of human life worldwide‘로 전환한 것은 알맞다.
ⓓ enter의 목적어인 명사구 human bodies를 관계사절인 ’that ~ viruses’가 수식하고 있으며 human bodies를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 that은 which로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으므로, that 대신 which를 사용해 ‘human bodies which have no prior immunity to such viruses’로 전환한 것은 알맞다.
ⓔ 앞의 완전한 절(These changes ~ wild animals)에 콤마(,)로 이어져 앞 절을 부연 설명하는 분사구문이므로 동일한 기능을 가지는 계속적 용법의 관계사절로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으며, 명사구 the viruses를 수식하는 형용사구 ‘present in wild animals’는 앞에 ‘주격 관계대명사+be동사’가 생략된 것으로 설명할 수 있다. 관계사절의 내용이 일반적 사실을 나타내고 선행사가 앞 절인 경우 단수 취급하므로, which 뒤에 현재시제이자 단수로 수일치한 means를 사용하고, present 앞에 선행사 the viruses에 어울리는 주격 관계대명사 which 또는 that 중 that을 사용하고, 선행사인 복수명사구에 수일치한 복수동사 are를 사용해, ‘which means more opportunities for the viruses that are present in wild animals to spread to humans’로 전환한 것은 알맞다.

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could (A)[keep / disrupt] the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
But they were (B)[right / wrong]. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and (C)[counter / multiply] bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: keep / right / counter
disrupt / wrong / multiply
keep / wrong / counter
disrupt / wrong / counter
disrupt / right / multiply
solution:
(A) 당시의 의사들이 흑사병의 원인이라고 생각했던 나쁜 공기에 대한 설명이므로, 몸의 내부 균형을 깨뜨린다는 흐름이 되는 disrupt(~에 지장을 주다, ~을 방해하다)가 알맞다.
keep ~을 유지하다
(B) they가 가리키는 1600년대 흑사병을 치료했던 의사들이 흑사병의 원인이 나쁜 공기라고 생각하고 마스크의 허브가 공기를 걸러내 병에 걸리지 않게 보호해 주길 바랐다고 했으나, 뒤에 흑사병이 실제로는 동물에서 사람으로 퍼질 수 있는 박테리아에 의해 발생했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 당시 의사들의 생각이 틀렸었다는 흐름이 되는 wrong(틀린, 잘못된)이 알맞다.
right 옳은
(C) 1600년대에 의사들이 사용한 의복과 방법은 실제로 흑사병으로부터 그들을 보호하지 못했지만 이후 상황이 크게 바뀌었다고 했으므로, 현대 의학으로 인해 이제 우리는 박테리아와 바이러스를 신속하게 탐지하고 그것을 예방할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 counter(~을 저지하다, ~에 대응하다)가 알맞다.
multiply ~을 증식시키다

When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick. The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could (A)[keep / disrupt] the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
But they were (B)[right / wrong]. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.
Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and (C)[counter / multiply] bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: new viruses as major subjects of research in modern medicine
the dedication of medical professionals who have fought invisible enemies
historical changes in ways of understanding and responding to infectious diseases
misconceptions about the spread and prevention of the plague in the 17th century
the advantages and disadvantages of plague doctors’ costumes in the 17th century
solution:
1600년대 흑사병에 대한 의사들의 잘못된 믿음 및 대처 방식과 그 이후로 오늘날까지 전염병의 이해와 대응과 관련해 의학이 얼마나 발전했는지를 다루고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ③ ‘전염병을 이해하고 대응하는 방식의 역사적 변화’가 알맞다.
오답
① 현대 의학에서 주 연구의 대상인 새로운 바이러스들
② 보이지 않는 적과 싸워 온 의료 전문가들의 헌신
④ 17세기 흑사병의 전파와 예방에 관한 오해
⑤ 17세기 흑사병 의사들의 복장의 장단점

body:
As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing them in the battle against diseases are arising. Of notable interest are the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment.
(A) Genes can be compared to instruction guides that govern how our bodies function. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, which can lead to health problems.
(B) In this process, specially modified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, it can potentially help the body fight off certain diseases.
(C) Gene therapy steps in to fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering corrected genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, enabling them to function properly.
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 바이러스에 대한 과학적 지식의 확장에 따라 질병과의 전쟁에 바이러스를 활용할 기회가 생겨나고 있으며 주목할 분야로 유전자 치료와 암 치료를 언급한 주어진 글에 이어, 유전자가 우리 몸이 기능하는 방식을 규정하는 지침서와 같다는 개념적인 설명과 함께 때로 사람들이 유전적 장애를 가지고 태어나며 이것이 건강 문제를 일으킬 수 있다고 언급하는 (A), 앞에 언급된 문제 상황을 these issues(이러한 문제들)로 가리켜 유전자 치료가 이 문제들을 해결하기 위해 개입하고, 치료의 핵심은 환자의 세포에 수정된 유전적 지침을 전달해 세포가 제대로 기능하게 하는 것이라고 설명한 (C), 앞서 설명한 유전자 치료의 과정을 this process(이러한 과정)로 가리켜, 이 과정에서 특수하게 변형된 바이러스가 유전적 지시를 전달하는 매개체 중 하나로 사용된다고 부연 설명한 (B)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses did not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans to survive.
Insect species populations are also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses that infect those insects also increase, reducing their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects to flourish. Considering the chain of food in nature, it would not be difficult to assume that viruses fulfill important functions in regulating other species. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.
다음 글의 요지를 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 각각 쓰시오.
Viruses play an important role in maintaining ______ by providing ______ to the Earth and regulating ______ species populations.
solution: 제시문 바이러스는 지구에 산소를 공급하고 곤충 종의 개체수를 조절함으로써 생태계를 유지하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.

body:
W: What would happen if all the fish in the world suddenly vanished? First, people around the world would face food shortages. Millions of people living near coastal areas live on fish. If all fish were gone, people might face starvation due to lack of food. Second, Earth’s carbon levels would increase. The oceans store a huge amount of carbon. Tiny marine plants absorb carbon, and fish eat them. Fish then swim down and store the carbon deep in the ocean. Without fish, Earth’s carbon levels would increase, worsening climate change.

다음 담화를 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 지문에서 찾아 알맞게 쓰시오. (필요시 변형하고, 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것)

If all fish suddenly disappeared, ______ ______ would emerge, and rising carbon levels would ______ climate change.
solution: [요약문] 모든 물고기가 갑자기 사라진다면, 식량 부족이 발생할 것이며, 증가하는 탄소 수치는 기후 변화를 악화시킬 것이다.

body:
Earle ⓐwas appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to ⓑprioritize ocean research and conservation. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. ⓒReturning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express ⓓher. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience ⓔto campaign for the ocean’s conservation.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Earle’s commitment to expanding public access to marine resources
Earle’s success in reforming NOAA’s approach to ocean development
difficulties Earle had in balancing scientific research with public responsibilities

body:
In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Earle walked on the seafloor at a depth of 381 meters for two hours without a cable.
As Earle moved deeper into the ocean, she was captivated by the creatures that glittered like stars in the darkness.
Earle confirmed that the deep-sea squid she had studied released a glowing liquid to attract prey.
Earle placed a flag on the ocean floor to highlight the importance of ocean exploration, linking the moment to Neil Armstrong’s first step on the Moon.
Earle’s accomplishment paved the way for humanity to appreciate and value life beneath the sea.
solution: Earle이 매료된 생물들 중에는 자신을 방어하기 위해 빛나는 액체를 내뿜는 심해 오징어와 같이 이전에 연구했지만 한 번도 본 적이 없는 종들도 있었다고 했으므로, ❸ ‘Earle은 그녀가 연구했던 심해 오징어가 먹이를 유인하기 위해 빛나는 액체를 방출했다는 것을 확인했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

body:
Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, increasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis.
(A) Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, rethinking industrial fishing practices, restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution entering the sea. By prioritizing ocean health, we can ⓐ[constrain / unlock] its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.
(B) Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes have been found to ⓑ[surpass / fall behind] plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean.
(C) Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that has dissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a ⓒ[beneficial / detrimental] material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming. Nevertheless, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet saving function depends on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and aid in the planet’s decarbonization.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 기후 변화로 인해 해양은 심각한 피해를 입기도 하지만, 동시에 이러한 글로벌 위기의 잠재적 해결책이 될 수 있다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 바다가 기후 위기의 해결책이 될 수 있다는 내용에 대해 바다가 대기 중 이산화탄소를 포집하고 저장하는 데 중요한 역할을 하며, 육지보다 훨씬 많은 탄소, 흔히 ‘블루 카본’이라는 것을 보유한다는 구체적인 근거를 제시하는 (B), 앞서 언급된 ‘블루 카본’의 의미를 ‘블랙 카본’과 비교해 설명한 뒤, 지구 보호 기능을 수행하는 해양의 능력이 그것의 건강에 달려 있으며 그에 따라 Duarte 박사와 그의 팀은 해양 건강의 회복 및 지구의 탈탄소화를 돕기 위한 실행 가능한 행동 계획을 제안한다는 내용의 (C), Duarte 박사와 그의 팀을 Their로 가리켜 그들이 제안하는 긴급한 권고 사항이 포함하는 내용을 구체적으로 설명하고 기후 변화에 대한 해결책으로서 해양 건강을 우선시해야 할 필요성을 강조하면서 마무리한 (A)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: constrain surpass detrimental
unlock surpass detrimental
constrain fall behind beneficial
unlock surpass beneficial
unlock fall behind detrimental
solution:
ⓐ 해양이 기후 변화로 인한 글로벌 위기의 잠재적 해결책이라고 했으므로, 해양을 건강하게 유지함으로써 기대되는 효과로서, 기후 변화에 대한 해결책으로서 해양의 잠재력을 이끌어 낼 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 unlock((잠재력 등)을 끌어내다)이 알맞다.
ⓑ 지구의 70%를 차지하는 바다는 대기 중 이산화탄소를 포집하는 데 중요한 역할을 하며, 육지보다 16배나 많은 탄소를 보유하고 있다고 설명하므로, 해양 생태계가 탄소를 포집하고 저장하는 데 있어 육지 식물을 능가한다는 흐름이 되는 surpass(~을 능가하다, ~보다 뛰어나다)가 알맞다.
ⓒ 블루 카본은 해양에 저장되어 지구 온난화를 방지한다는 사실과 대조되는 내용이 While(~한 반면)에 의해 이어져야 하며, 화석 연료를 태울 때 발생한다는 설명이 함께 언급되므로, 블랙 카본은 해로운 물질로서 기후 변화의 주요 원인이 된다는 흐름이 되는 detrimental(유해한)이 알맞다.

W: Hello, Mr. Hopkins. I’m wondering if you can help me design a poster for the special lecture hosted by the school council.
M: Okay, what’s the lecture about?

Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. ⓓHaving moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. ⓒ 앞에 나온 명사의 반복을 피하기 위해 쓰인 지시대명사로, 흐름상 단수명사 attention을 대신하므로 단수형인 that이 알맞다.

However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes have been found to ⓑexceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as “blue carbon,” absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that has ⓒdissolved directly in the ocean. While “black carbon” is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming.
Nevertheless, the ocean’s ability to perform this planet ⓓsaving function depends on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and aid in the planet’s decarbonization. Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, ⓔencouraging industrial fishing practices, restoring damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution entering the sea. In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. ⓐHaving used the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures ⓑthat flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them ⓒwas some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor ⓓto symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and ⓔnoted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day ⓕwhich human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ Having used → Using (완전한 절(she dove ~ for two hours) 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰인 분사구문을 이루는 분사(구)가 올 수 있으며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the JIM suit가 있으므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사(구)가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주절의 과거 시점보다 앞선 시점이 아닌 같은 시점에서 일어나는 상황이므로 Having p.p. 형태의 Having used를 Using으로 고친다.)
ⓒ was → were (부사구 Among them이 강조를 위해 문두에 쓰이면서 부사구 도치에 의해 흐름상 과거시제의 be동사가 주어 앞에 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 주어 some species가 복수명사구이므로 수일치를 위해 단수동사 was를 복수동사 were로 고친다.)
ⓕ which → on which 또는 when[that] 또는 which 삭제 (완전한 절(human beings ~ underwater)을 이끌어 선행사인 시간 명사구 the day를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 which를 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 쓴 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태의 on which로 고치거나 관계부사 when으로 고친다. 또한 선행사가 time, day, year와 같은 일반적 시간을 나타내는 명사일 때 관계부사 when 대신 관계부사 대용의 that을 쓰거나 생략할 수 있으므로, that으로 고치거나 which를 삭제하는 것도 가능하다.)
*원래 지문에는 when이 쓰였음
오답
ⓔ 주어 She에 대한 첫 번째 과거동사 associated와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 있으며, 뒤에 목적어로 인용 부호(“ ”)와 함께 쓰인 명사절(“These ~ ocean.”)이 있으므로, 능동태 과거동사 noted는 알맞다.

firsthand 직접 체험으로
(B) 해양 보호 구역인 ‘Hope Spots’가 하는 역할로서 언급되어야 하므로, 오염, 남획 및 기타 위협으로부터 해양 생태계를 보호하는 역할을 한다는 흐름이 되는 refuges from(~로부터의 피난처)가 알맞다.
triggers for ~의 촉발 요인
(C) 미션 블루는 바다를 탐험하고 보호하기 위한 행동을 촉구하는 비영리단체로서 2030년까지 해양의 30%를 보호한다는 목표를 갖고 있다고 했으므로, 이러한 목표가 국제자연보전연맹(IUCN)이 해양 건강을 유지하기 위해 권장하는 목표에 부합하는 것이라는 흐름이 되는 maintaining(유지하는 것)이 알맞다.
worsening 악화시키는 것

body:
B: Hello, Ms. Han. Can I take a rest for a while? I don’t feel good.
W: Uhm, you have a fever and a runny nose. It seems that your immune system is working hard to protect your body.
B: Immune system? What is that exactly?
W: ______ the body system that helps fight against germs causing diseases.
B: But what does the runny nose have to do with the immune system?
W: When you’re sick, your body produces more liquid inside your nose to wash the germs away.
B: I see. Then, what’s the deal with the fever? Why does my body get all hot?
W: Your body heats up because viruses or bacteria cannot survive above the normal body temperature.
B: Is there anything I can do to boost my immune system?
W: Absolutely! Eat a healthy diet, get regular exercise, manage your stress level, and get enough sleep.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞지 않은 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: It means
It refers to
It results from
It is caused by
It is defined as
solution:
소년이 면역 체계가 정확히 무엇인지 물었고, 이에 대한 대답으로 ‘병을 일으키는 균과 싸우는 것을 돕는 신체 시스템’이라는 정의를 언급하고 있으므로, 어떤 용어나 개념의 정의를 제시할 때 사용하는 표현이 빈칸에 와야 한다. 따라서 인과관계를 설명할 때 쓰이는 표현인 ③ ‘It results from ~(그것은 ~에 기인해)’과 ④ ’It is caused by ~(그것은 ~에 의해 야기돼)‘는 빈칸에 알맞지 않다.
오답
① 그것은 ~을 의미해
② 그것은 ~을 나타내
⑤ 그것은 ~로 정의돼

body:
It appears (A)[that / what] viruses exist solely to bring suffering to humanity. The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated (B)[to kill / to have killed] 50 to 100 million people. Smallpox claimed the lives of a further 200 million people in the 20th century alone, according to estimates. And of course, the recent COVID-19 pandemic has taken several million lives, (C)[affecting / affected] almost every aspect of human life worldwide.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: that / to kill / affecting
what / to kill / affected
that / to have killed / affected
what / to kill / affecting
that / to have killed / affecting
solution:
(A) 가주어 It에 대한 진주어 자리에서 완전한 절(viruses exist ~ humanity)을 이끌고 있으므로, ‘It appears that+완전한 절(~한 것처럼 보이다)’ 형태의 가주어-진주어 구문을 이루는 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.
(B) ‘~한 것으로 추정되다’라는 뜻의 ‘be estimated+to부정사(구)’에서 추정되는 시점이 현재이므로 현재시제 is estimated가 쓰였으나 사람들이 사망한 것은 과거의 일이며, to부정사(구)의 내용이 본동사의 시제보다 이전 상황이면 완료부정사(to have p.p.)를 사용하므로, to have killed가 알맞다.
(C) 앞의 완전한 절(the recent ~ lives)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이끄는 분사가 올 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 the recent COVID-19 pandemic이 ‘영향을 미치는’ 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구(almost every aspect of human life)가 이어져 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 affecting이 알맞다.

body:
ⓐWhat is less commonly known is that viruses play crucial roles in supporting much of life on Earth. This is because researchers have only recently begun investigating the viruses that sustain us and the planet, instead of just ⓑthose that harm us. Therefore, scientists have ⓒmuch more to learn about viruses than they currently know. (A)그들이 정말로 알고 있는 것은 바이러스가 박테리아와 곤충 개체군의 주요 조절자의 역할을 한다는 것이다.
Since viruses do not have reproductive functions on their own, they steal the reproductive functions of other organisms ⓓto multiply. Some types of viruses use bacteria. When the virus continues to multiply inside the bacteria, the bacteria eventually die, and the newly produced viruses go on to infect other bacteria. This whole process helps viruses ⓔcontrolling the excessive growth of certain bacteria.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ controlling → (to) control (‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식 구문에서 준사역동사 help의 목적격보어로 to부정사나 동사원형이 쓰이므로, controlling을 to control이나 control로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 control이 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 불완전한 절 ‘is less commonly known’과 문장의 본동사 is, 보어절인 that절(that viruses play ~ on Earth)이 이어지므로, 문장의 주어 자리에서 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 불완전한 절을 이끌어 명사절을 이루는 관계대명사 What은 알맞다.
ⓑ 흐름상 복수명사구 the viruses를 대신해 쓰인 복수형 지시대명사 those는 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 비교급(more)을 강조하기 위해 쓰인 much는 알맞다.
ⓓ 앞의 완전한 절(they steal ~ other organisms)에 ‘증식하기 위해’라는 의미로 이어져야 하므로, ‘크게 증가하다’라는 의미의 자동사 multiply를 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to multiply로 쓴 것은 알맞다.

body:
ⓐOutbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter human bodies that have no prior ⓑimmunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has ⓒdestroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in a ⓓdecrease in interactions between human and wild animals, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may ⓔincrease in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓓ a decrease(감소) → an increase(증가)

body:
The greater significance of viruses infecting bacteria is that they play a vital role in supplying oxygen to our planet. About half of the oxygen on Earth is produced by plankton in the oceans, and the primary food source for these plankton is nutrients released from bacteria killed by viral infections. If viruses did not infect and kill bacteria, there would be no bacterial remains, leading to a lack of plankton. Without plankton, half of Earth’s oxygen would disappear. In short, without viruses, the lack of oxygen would make it impossible for humans to survive.
Insect species populations are also regulated by viruses. When a specific type of insect increases excessively, the viruses that infect those insects also increase, reducing their numbers. This, in turn, creates room for other types of insects to flourish. Considering the chain of food in nature, it would not be difficult to assume that viruses fulfill important functions in ______. We have just started to understand their various roles in the ecosystem.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: producing oxygen
regulating other species
causing genetic mutations
supporting the growth of all species
helping different organisms fairly compete for limited resources
solution:
특정 유형의 곤충이 과도하게 증가하면 해당 곤충을 감염시키는 바이러스도 증가하여 그 곤충의 수가 감소하며, 이는 다른 종류의 곤충이 번성할 여지를 만들어준다고 설명했으므로, 자연의 먹이 사슬을 고려할 때 바이러스가 다른 종을 조절하는 중요한 기능을 수행한다는 것을 가정할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② '다른 종들을 조절하는 것'이 알맞다.
오답
① 산소를 생성하는 것
③ 유전적 돌연변이를 일으키는 것
④ 모든 종의 성장을 지원하는 것
⑤ 서로 다른 생물들이 제한된 자원을 두고 공정하게 경쟁하도록 돕는 것

윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Viruses themselves are responsible for roughly half of Earth’s oxygen production.

solution:
플랑크톤의 주요 먹이는 바이러스 감염으로 죽은 박테리아에서 방출된 영양소라고 했으므로, ② '플랑크톤은 바이러스 감염에 의해 파괴된 박테리아에서 나온 영양분을 먹이로 삼는다.'는 글의 내용과 일치한다.
오답
① 바이러스 자체가 지구의 약 절반의 산소 생산을 담당한다.(→바이러스가 아닌 바다의 플랑크톤이 지구의 산소의 약 절반을 생산한다.)
③ 바이러스가 없음에도 불구하고 인류의 생존은 가능할 것이다.(→바이러스가 없으면 산소 부족으로 인간의 생존이 불가능할 것이다.)
④ 바이러스는 몇몇 곤충 개체군의 빠른 증가에 기여할 수 있다.(→바이러스는 과도하게 증가한 특정 유형의 곤충의 수를 줄이는 역할을 한다.)
⑤ 인간은 이제 바이러스가 생태계에서 수행하는 다양한 역할에 대한 완전한 이해를 가지고 있다.(→인간은 바이러스가 수행하는 다양한 역할을 이제 막 이해하기 시작했다.)

body:
Another less recognized role of viruses is their contribution to the evolution of life on Earth. When a virus infects a reproductive cell of its host, such as an egg or sperm, the viral DNA may be passed down to the host’s offspring. The insertion of new DNA into genomes is a significant mechanism of evolution. Without viruses, in other words, the evolutionary potential for all life on the planet would be (A)[impacted / unaffected].
One example of viruses’ contributions to evolution is their role in the development of the placenta in mammals. A placenta is a complex organ that helps the fetus grow securely inside its mother’s body. It (B)[facilitates / inhibits] the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products while protecting the fetus from the mother’s immune system. In the early days of evolution, female animals had to leave their offspring in one location, like eggs in a nest, making them (C)[vulnerable / invulnerable] to predators. After the emergence of the placenta, females were able to carry their young inside their bodies safely from one location to another. Viruses that infected our remote ancestors more than 130 million years ago have been reported to have served a key function in the development of this vital organ.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: impacted / facilitates / vulnerable
impacted / inhibits / vulnerable
impacted / facilitates / invulnerable
unaffected / facilitates / invulnerable
unaffected / inhibits / vulnerable
solution:
(A) 바이러스가 숙주의 생식 세포를 감염시키면 바이러스의 DNA가 숙주의 자손에게 전달될 수 있으며, 새로운 DNA가 게놈에 삽입되는 것은 진화의 중요한 메커니즘이라고 했으므로, 바이러스가 없다면 지구상의 모든 생명체의 진화 잠재력이 영향을 받게 될 것이라는 흐름이 되는 impacted(영향을 받는)가 알맞다.
unaffected 영향을 받지 않은
(B) 태반은 태아가 엄마의 몸 안에서 안전하게 성장할 수 있도록 돕는 기관이라고 했으므로, 그것이 산소, 영양분, 노폐물의 교환을 용이하게 한다는 흐름이 되는 facilitates(~을 용이하게 하다)가 알맞다.
inhibits ~을 억제[방해]하다
(C) 진화 초기에는 암컷이 새끼를 한 곳에 두어야만 했다는 이유가 앞에 제시되었으며, 뒤에는 태반의 출현 이후 암컷이 새끼를 몸 안에 넣어 한 장소에서 다른 장소로 안전하게 옮길 수 있게 되었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 포식자의 공격에 취약했다는 흐름이 되는 vulnerable(공격받기 쉬운)이 알맞다.
invulnerable (공격 등에) 끄떡없는, 영향을 받지 않는

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick.
(A) The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
(B) The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
(C) Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
(D) But they were wrong. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 1600년대 유럽에서 흑사병이 발병했을 때 의사들이 환자를 치료하기 위해 기묘한 복장을 입었다고 언급한 주어진 글에 이어, 그 복장의 구성에 대해 구체적으로 묘사한 (B), 의상에서 가장 특이한 부분이었던 마스크와 의사들이 그것을 착용한 이유로 흑사병이 나쁜 공기로 인해 발생한다고 생각했다고 언급한 (A), But(하지만)을 사용해 앞서 언급된 의사들의 생각이 틀렸다는 대조적인 내용을 연결 후, 실제로 흑사병의 원인이 박테리아였음을 밝힌 (D), 앞서 언급한 과거 상황을 then(그 때)으로 가리켜 그 이후 상황이 크게 바뀌었고, 현대 의학으로 인해 박테리아와 바이러스를 신속하게 탐지하고 대응할 수 있게 되었으며, 보호 장비가 우리를 바이러스에서 보호해준다고 설명한 (C)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

body:
When a deadly disease called the plague killed many people in Europe in the 1600s, some doctors wore a strange costume to treat the sick.
(A) The most unusual part of the costume was the mask: It had glasses and a long nose like a bird’s beak, which was filled with herbs and other things that smelled good. The doctors thought that the plague was caused by bad air that could disrupt the body’s internal balance. They hoped that the herbs in the mask would filter the air and protect them from getting sick.
(B) The costume had a long coat with polish on it and pants and boots that were attached. Their shirts were fastened, and they wore hats and gloves made of goat skin. The doctors also had a stick that they used to touch or push away the sick people.
(C) Things have greatly changed since then. With modern medicine, we detect and counter bacteria and viruses swiftly. Protective gear protects us during virus research and patient treatment. Yet, our reliance on brave doctors and scientists remains unchanged, as they combat unseen enemies to protect humanity.
(D) But they were wrong. The plague was caused by bacteria that could spread from animals to people. The bacteria could also spread through flea bites or contact with sick people. The doctors’ costume and methods did not really protect them from the plague.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Doctors treating the plague in 17th century Europe wore masks filled with herbs and pleasant-smelling substances.
Doctors believed that the plague resulted from bad air.
Humanity’s trust in medical experts has continued to this day.
The true cause of the plague was a bacterium that easily spread from person to person.
The clothing worn by doctors treating the plague was actually ineffective in preventing infection.
solution:
의사들은 흑사병이 몸의 내부 균형을 깨뜨릴 수 있는 나쁜 공기 때문에 발생한다고 생각했지만 틀렸고, 흑사병은 동물에서 사람으로 퍼질 수 있는 박테리아에 의해 발생했다고 했으므로, ④ ‘흑사병의 진짜 원인은 사람 간에 쉽게 전염되는 박테리아였다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 17세기 유럽에서 흑사병을 치료한 의사들은 허브와 좋은 냄새가 나는 물질로 채워진 마스크를 착용했다.
② 의사들은 흑사병의 원인이 나쁜 공기에서 비롯된다고 생각했다.
③ 의학 전문가들에 대한 인류의 신뢰는 오늘날까지 이어져 오고 있다.
⑤ 흑사병을 치료하던 의사들의 복장은 실제로 예방 효과가 없었다.

We have yet to find out how many virus types even exist, let alone the characteristics of each of them. The more we learn about viruses, however, the better equipped we will be to use certain viruses for beneficial purposes and to develop defenses against viruses that could lead to the next pandemic. More than that, learning more about viral diversity will help us reach a deeper understanding of the working of our planet, ecosystems, and our own bodies.

choices: the need to identify unknown types of virus

body:
As scientific knowledge about viruses continues to expand, new opportunities for utilizing them in the battle against diseases are arising. Of notable interest are the areas of gene therapy and cancer treatment. Genes can be compared to instruction guides that govern how our bodies function. Sometimes, people are born with genetic disorders, which can lead to health problems. Gene therapy steps in to fix these issues. The essence of gene therapy lies in delivering corrected genetic instructions to a patient’s cells, enabling them to function properly. In this process, specially modified viruses are used as one of the carriers of the genetic instructions. If the patient’s cells function properly, it can potentially help the body fight off certain diseases.
Using viruses to treat cancer, another use of viruses, is based on the notion of utilizing their natural ability to infect and kill cells. If successful, viruses can be manipulated to specifically target and destroy cancer cells while leaving healthy cells unharmed. The use of viruses in gene therapy and cancer treatment is still in the early stages. However, many researchers are involved in hundreds of projects with the goal of discovering cures for diseases that were once thought to be incurable.

윗글의 요지를 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 지문에서 찾아 알맞게 쓰시오. (각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것)
The expansion of ______ ______ is creating ______ to use viruses as a means of treating ______.
solution: 제시문 과학적 지식의 확장은 질병 치료의 수단으로서 바이러스를 활용할 기회를 만들고 있다.

body:
Outbreaks of viral diseases are frequently linked to contact with wild animals such as bats. Such contacts allow new viruses to enter human bodies that have no prior immunity to such viruses. Historically, natural barriers such as mountains and forests prevented animal viruses from infecting humans. Industrialization has destroyed these barriers, and climate change has pushed some wild animals out of their original habitats. These changes have resulted in an increase in interactions between human and wild animals, meaning more opportunities for the viruses present in wild animals to spread to humans. This is the primary reason for scientists’ concern that pandemics may increase in the future. Then, is the virus truly a harmful presence to humans? Not necessarily.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
The (A)______ of natural barriers between humans and wildlife caused by industrialization and climate change (B)______ the risk of new viruses being transmitted to humans through contact with wildlife.
(A) (B)
choices: preservation / increases
destruction / increases
preservation / decreases
destruction / eliminates
strengthening / decreases
